notes.example:
/tə tʃeɪz ʌp/
Formalnie (OET): to follow up on / to enquire about the status of

I'll chase up the estate agent about the contract tomorrow.
Can you chase up that MRI referral? It's been two weeks.
She chased up the lab results and they finally came back.

/tə kræk ɒn/
Formalnie (OET): to proceed with / to continue with / to get on with

Right, I'll crack on — lots to get through today.
We cracked on with the list despite being short-staffed.
I can't stop long — I need to crack on with these reports.

/tə fɒb ˈsʌmwʌn ɒf/
Formalnie (OET): to dismiss / to deflect / to give an evasive response

The council keeps fobbing me off with excuses.
Don't let them fob you off — ask to speak to the manager.
I felt like I was being fobbed off without a proper explanation.

/tə pɒp tə ðə ʃɒps/
Formalnie (OET): to go to the shops / to visit the pharmacy

I'm just popping to the shops — need anything?
She popped to the pharmacy on her lunch break.
I'll pop out and grab some coffee before the meeting starts.

/ɪts ˈtɪpɪŋ ɪt daʊn/
Formalnie (OET): it's raining heavily / there's heavy rainfall

Don't go out yet — it's tipping it down.
It was tipping it down all morning, so the car park was chaos.
I got soaked — it just started tipping it down out of nowhere.

/tə biː ˈɡʌtɪd/
Formalnie (OET): to be very disappointed / to be devastated

I was absolutely gutted when I heard the news.
He was gutted to miss the procedure after preparing all week.
You must be gutted — that's such a disappointing result.

/tə sɔːt ˈsʌmθɪŋ aʊt/
Formalnie (OET): to resolve / to arrange / to deal with

I'll sort out the paperwork before the end of the day.
Can you sort out a bed for the new admission?
We sorted it out between us — no need to escalate.

/feər ɪˈnʌf/
Formalnie (OET): I understand / that's reasonable / I can see the reasoning

Fair enough — I can see why you'd want a second opinion.
Fair enough, let's give it another 24 hours.
Fair enough — I'll rebook for next week then.

/tə biː ʌp fə ˈsʌmθɪŋ/
Formalnie (OET): to be willing to / to be happy to / to be available for

Are you up for a coffee after the ward round?
Is anyone up for covering Saturday morning?
I'm up for it if the rest of the team agrees.

/tə biː tʃʌft/
Formalnie (OET): to be very pleased / to be delighted / to be thrilled

She was absolutely chuffed with her exam results.
The patient was chuffed to hear he could go home.
I'm really chuffed we managed to finish on time.

/tə biː ˈnækəd/
Formalnie (OET): to be exhausted / to be very tired

I'm absolutely knackered — that was a brutal shift.
He looked knackered; I don't think he'd slept at all.
Don't ask me to stay late tonight — I'm completely knackered.

notes.front: to be run off one's feet
notes.back: nie móc złapać oddechu / być zawalonym
notes.example:
/tə biː rʌn ɒf wʌnz fiːt/
Formalnie (OET): to be extremely busy / to have an exceptionally heavy workload

Sorry I didn't call back — I've been run off my feet all day.
The A&E team was completely run off their feet last night.
We've been run off our feet since the new admissions policy changed.

/ə bɪt əv ə ˈnaɪtmeə/
Formalnie (OET): rather challenging / quite problematic / far from straightforward

Parking near the hospital is a bit of a nightmare.
The handover was a bit of a nightmare — three unexpected admissions.
Getting the IT system to work has been a bit of a nightmare, honestly.

notes.front: to get the hang of something
notes.back: łapać rytm / ogarniać jak coś działa
notes.example:
/tə ɡet ðə hæŋ əv ˈsʌmθɪŋ/
Formalnie (OET): to become familiar with / to master / to grow accustomed to

It took me a while, but I'm finally getting the hang of the EPR system.
Once you get the hang of it, the commute isn't bad at all.
Don't worry — you'll get the hang of the ward routine within a week.

/tə tʌtʃ beɪs/
Formalnie (OET): to contact / to follow up with / to liaise with

I'll touch base with the ward sister before I leave.
Can we touch base tomorrow morning before the MDT?
I just wanted to touch base and see how you're settling in.

/beə wɪð miː/
Formalnie (OET): one moment please / please allow me a moment

Bear with me — I just need to pull up your notes.
Bear with me for a moment while I check the scan results.
Bear with me — the system is running slowly this morning.

/tə ɡɪv ˈsʌmwʌn ə ˈhedz ʌp/
Formalnie (OET): to notify in advance / to inform beforehand / to alert

Just wanted to give you a heads-up — the patient in bay four is quite anxious.
Thanks for the heads-up about the ward closure.
Can you give me a heads-up before you send the referral?

notes.front: to be in the same boat
notes.back: być w tej samej sytuacji / mieć ten sam problem
notes.example:
/tə biː ɪn ðə seɪm bəʊt/
Formalnie (OET): to be in a similar situation / to face the same challenges

We're all in the same boat with the parking situation.
Everyone here is in the same boat — new city, new system.
I know it's tough, but we're all in the same boat right now.

/tə ˈfænsi/
Formalnie (OET): would you like / would you be interested in

Do you fancy a coffee before the ward round?
I don't fancy another night on call so soon.
Do you fancy trying that new Italian place near the station?

/tə nɪp aʊt/
Formalnie (OET): to step out briefly / to go out for a moment

I'm just nipping out to grab a sandwich — back in ten minutes.
She nipped to the pharmacy on her lunch break.
Can I nip out for five minutes? I need to make a call.

/tə kʌm əˈkrɒs æz/
Formalnie (OET): to appear / to seem / to present as

He came across as quite anxious during the consultation.
She comes across as very capable — I think she'll fit in well.
I hope I didn't come across as dismissive — that wasn't my intention.

notes.back: nie wyjść po bożemu / wziąć w łeb
notes.example:
/tə ɡəʊ ˈpeəʃeɪpt/
Formalnie (OET): to go wrong / to deteriorate unexpectedly / to fail

The plan was fine, but things went pear-shaped in theatre.
It all went pear-shaped when the second cannula failed.
The day started well, then went completely pear-shaped after lunch.

notes.back: nadrobić zaległości / spotkać się po czasie
notes.example:
/tə kætʃ ʌp/
Formalnie (OET): to meet / to reconnect / to review progress with

Let's catch up properly after the MDT meeting.
I need to catch up on my paperwork before Friday.
It was great to catch up with the cardiology team at the conference.

/tə ˈrekən/
Formalnie (OET): to think / to believe / in my view / in my opinion

I reckon we should keep him in overnight just to be safe.
What do you reckon — is she ready for discharge?
I reckon the scan will come back clear, but let's wait and see.

/tə rɪŋ ˈsʌmwʌn/
Formalnie (OET): to telephone / to contact / to call

I'll ring the registrar and let them know.
Ring me if anything changes overnight.
She rang ahead to warn us the patient was on his way in.

/dʌz ðæt sjuːt juː/
Formalnie (OET): would that be convenient / would that work for you

I've booked the scan for Thursday — does that suit you?
We could meet at two o'clock — does that suit you?
I'll schedule the follow-up for next Tuesday — does that suit?

notes.front: to get on (with someone / with something)
notes.example:
/tə ɡet ɒn wɪð/
Formalnie (OET): to manage / to cope with / to progress with

How are you getting on with the new medication?
How are you getting on with the EPR system?
He gets on well with everyone on the team.

/tʃɪəz/
Formalnie (OET): thank you / many thanks / I'm very grateful

Cheers for covering my bleep.
Cheers — I'll see you at handover.
Cheers for that, really helpful.

/tə hæv ə ɡəʊ/
Formalnie (OET): to attempt / to try

Do you want to have a go at cannulating first?
Have a go at writing up the discharge summary — I'll review it.
I had a go at fixing the printer but gave up in the end.

notes.back: wszystko mi jedno / nie mam zdania
notes.example:
/aɪm nɒt ˈbɒðəd/
Formalnie (OET): I have no preference / either would be fine / I'm happy with either

Tea or coffee? — I'm not bothered, either is fine.
Window seat or aisle? — I'm not bothered.
Which consultant covers it? — Honestly, I'm not bothered either way.

notes.back: Czy mogę…? / Czy ma Pan/Pani coś przeciwko?
notes.example:
/duː juː maɪnd ɪf/
Formalnie (OET): may I / would it be alright if / would you be comfortable if

Do you mind if I examine your abdomen?
Do you mind if I ask a colleague to join us?
Do you mind if I open the window? It's quite warm in here.

/ˈkæri ɒn/
Formalnie (OET): please continue / do continue / please proceed

Carry on — I didn't mean to interrupt.
Carry on with the examination; I'll just observe.
Sorry to keep you waiting — please carry on.

/æz ɪt ˈhæpənz/
Formalnie (OET): as it turns out / coincidentally / it so happens that

As it happens, I know that area quite well.
As it happens, we had a very similar case last week.
As it happens, the consultant is available this afternoon.

/aɪ mʌst seɪ/
Formalnie (OET): I should note / I have to say / I find it noteworthy that

I must say, the flat is much bigger than I expected.
I must say, the team have handled this very well.
I must say, I wasn't expecting such a quick recovery.

notes.front: if you don't mind me asking
notes.back: jeśli mogę zapytać / nie chcąc być wścibskim
notes.example:
/ɪf juː dəʊnt maɪnd miː ˈɑːskɪŋ/
Formalnie (OET): if I may ask / may I enquire / if I may

If you don't mind me asking, how long have you been in the UK?
If you don't mind me asking, what brought you to see us today?
If you don't mind me asking, is there anything worrying you about the procedure?

/ðæt sed/
Formalnie (OET): however / nevertheless / nonetheless

It's a long commute. That said, the pay is very good.
The results aren't ideal. That said, we have good treatment options.
It's a complex case. That said, I'm cautiously optimistic.

/ɔːl ˈbiːɪŋ wel/
Formalnie (OET): subject to no complications / provided all proceeds as planned

All being well, you should be home by the weekend.
All being well, the results will be back by Thursday.
We'll discharge her tomorrow, all being well.

/tə biː ˈɒnɪst/
Formalnie (OET): frankly / to be candid / I should be transparent

To be honest, I found the commute more manageable than I thought.
To be honest, I'm not entirely sure — I'd want a second opinion.
To be honest with you, the prognosis is quite uncertain at this stage.

/aɪ dəʊnt səˈpəʊz juː kʊd/
Formalnie (OET): would you be able to / I wonder whether you could / could I ask you to

I don't suppose you could recommend a good GP in this area?
I don't suppose you could cover the ward for an hour?
I don't suppose you could take a look at this before the meeting?

notes.back: co prawda / ale z drugiej strony / swoją drogą
notes.example:
/maɪnd juː/
Formalnie (OET): however / I should note / that said

It's quite expensive to rent here. Mind you, the transport links are excellent.
It was a difficult case. Mind you, the outcome was better than expected.
The ward is busy. Mind you, it's always like this on a Monday.

notes.front: to take something in one's stride
notes.back: radzić sobie z czymś spokojnie / bez paniki
notes.example:
/tə teɪk ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɪn wʌnz straɪd/
Formalnie (OET): to manage / to cope with composure / to handle without difficulty

The paperwork was overwhelming at first, but she took it all in her stride.
He took the bad news remarkably well — completely in his stride.
Moving to a new country is hard, but you seem to be taking it in your stride.

/ˈkwɒlɪti əˈʃɔːd/
Formalnie (OET): verified / validated / meets the required standard

The equipment has been quality assured before theatre use.
All discharge summaries are quality assured by the consultant.
Your blood results are quality assured — you can trust them.

notes.back: sprowadza się to do… / w gruncie rzeczy chodzi o…
notes.example:
/ɪt bɔɪlz daʊn tə/
Formalnie (OET): ultimately / the fundamental issue is / in essence / the key consideration is

It boils down to whether the patient is willing to try the treatment.
In the end, it boils down to shared decision-making with the patient.
It boils down to resource constraints and prioritising urgent cases.

notes.back: zmienić kierunek / przestawić się na coś
notes.example:
/tə ˈpɪvət/
Formalnie (OET): to shift to / to transition to / to redirect our approach towards

We need to pivot our approach — the current plan isn't working.
The team pivoted to a palliative strategy after the latest scan results.
During the pandemic, many services pivoted to remote consultations.

notes.back: nieszczery / nieuczciwy w argumentacji / udający niewiedzę
notes.example:
/ˌdɪsɪnˈdʒenjuəs/
Formalnie (OET): insincere / misleading / lacking candour / not entirely candid

It would be disingenuous to claim that the evidence is conclusive — we need more data.
I think it's a little disingenuous to suggest that funding wasn't a factor in this decision.
To be disingenuous here would undermine the patient's trust entirely.

notes.front: to put someone in the picture
notes.example:
/tə pʊt ˈsʌmwʌn ɪn ðə ˈpɪktʃə/
Formalnie (OET): to brief / to inform / to update someone on the situation

Let me put you in the picture — there have been some changes to the rota.
I'll put the family in the picture once we have the results.
Can someone put the on-call team in the picture before handover?

notes.front: to be on the same page
notes.back: mieć wspólne rozumienie / być po tej samej stronie
notes.example:
/tə biː ɒn ðə seɪm peɪdʒ/
Formalnie (OET): to be in agreement / to share the same understanding

Before we proceed, I want to make sure we're all on the same page.
Let's just clarify the plan — I want to be on the same page as the family.
The MDT wasn't quite on the same page, so we deferred the decision.

notes.back: wziąć pod uwagę / przyjąć do wiadomości
notes.example:
/tə teɪk ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɒn bɔːd/
Formalnie (OET): to consider / to take into account / to acknowledge

Thank you for the feedback — I'll take that on board.
I've taken your concerns on board and we're reviewing the protocol.
She took the advice on board and made the changes straightaway.

notes.back: o ile mi wiadomo / według mojej wiedzy
notes.example:
/æz fɑː æz aɪm əˈweə/
Formalnie (OET): to my knowledge / based on the information available to me

As far as I'm aware, the scan results haven't come back yet.
As far as I'm aware, no one has spoken to the family today.
There are no contraindications, as far as I'm aware.

/tə biː taɪd ʌp/
Formalnie (OET): to be unavailable / to be occupied / to be otherwise engaged

The consultant is tied up in theatre — can I take a message?
I'm tied up until three, but I can call you back after that.
She was tied up with a complex case and couldn't attend the MDT.

notes.back: udać się / wypalić / dokonać czegoś trudnego
notes.example:
/tə pʊl ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɒf/
Formalnie (OET): to achieve / to accomplish / to succeed in / to carry out successfully

The procedure was technically demanding, but the team pulled it off.
I wasn't sure we'd manage the discharge by Friday, but we pulled it off.
He pulled off a very difficult conversation with the family — handled it beautifully.

notes.back: przeżyć / wyjść z tego / dać radę
notes.example:
/tə pʊl θruː/
Formalnie (OET): to survive / to recover / to make it through

Against all odds, he pulled through after the surgery.
She's pulled through some very dark times — she's remarkably strong.
We weren't sure he'd pull through, but he's stabilising well.

notes.back: przejść przez coś trudnego / wyjść z opałów
notes.example:
/tə kʌm θruː/
Formalnie (OET): to overcome / to get through / to emerge from

She's come through a very difficult year — she's incredibly resilient.
He came through the operation better than we expected.
It won't be easy, but I'm confident you'll come through this.

notes.back: doprowadzić do końca / wytrwać do końca
notes.example:
/tə siː ˈsʌmθɪŋ θruː/
Formalnie (OET): to complete / to follow through with / to persist with

It's a long treatment course, but I'd encourage you to see it through.
We started this together and we'll see it through.
He was determined to see the rehabilitation programme through despite the setbacks.

notes.back: ujść na sucho / przepchnąć coś bez konsekwencji
notes.example:
/tə ɡet əˈweɪ wɪð ˈsʌmθɪŋ/
Formalnie (OET): to succeed despite the risks / to avoid negative consequences

We got away with a conservative approach, which I wasn't expecting.
You can't always get away with delaying the decision — at some point you have to act.
We got away with it this time, but the protocol needs updating.

notes.back: przeprowadzić coś z sukcesem / dokonać czegoś trudnego
notes.example:
/tə brɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɒf/
Formalnie (OET): to accomplish / to carry out successfully / to achieve

It was a complicated case — I wasn't sure we'd bring it off.
The team brought off a really difficult intervention under pressure.
She brought it off brilliantly — the family were very reassured.
